key_insight: ERCPMP-Gx introduces a new endoscopic dataset centered on hereditary colorectal polyposis, linking image and video data with morphological, histopathological, and genomic labels. This creates a multi-level resource for studying how visible polyp appearance relates to underlying disease subtype and genetics.
problem_solved: Existing public endoscopic datasets mostly focus on isolated sporadic polyps and do not connect the polyposis phenotype to histopathology or genomic information. This paper addresses the lack of an integrated dataset for early identification and classification of hereditary polyposis syndromes.
method: Curates endoscopic images and videos of colorectal polyposis cases into a structured research dataset.
Annotates data with morphological, histopathological, and genomic characterization for richer supervision.
Organizes the resource to support AI models for syndrome classification, phenotype-genotype analysis, and surveillance research.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this dataset enables multimodal learning beyond simple polyp detection, supporting clinically meaningful tasks like subtype classification and biomarker discovery. It also improves the realism and translational value of models used in colorectal cancer prevention.

paper_title: ERCPMP-Gx: Endoscopic Image and Video Dataset for Morphological, Histopathological, and Genomic Characterization of Colorectal Polyposis
paper_authors: Zahra Ghaffari, Massih Bahar, Mojgan Forootan, Ali Darvishi, Hamidreza Bolhasani
